newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS-Brazil shares recover from last week's rout.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Brazil shares recover from last week's rout.

text.p: Brazilian stocks on Tuesday recouped much of last week's heavy losses, surging over eight percent as domestic and foreign investors returned to the Sao Paulo bolsa looking for bargains, analysts said.
But experts expected shares to remain volatile in the short term as the bolsa sought new levels before stabilizing and moving moderately higher in the last half of the year.
"We are still in the middle of great volatility, which is likely to last for the next two weeks," said Luis Eduardo de Assis, Investments Director at Citibank Brazil.
Share prices rose 0.98 percent Monday and 8.35 percent Tuesday, reducing last week's 15 percent loss to 6.9 percent.
The Bovespa index .BVSP, which before last week's retreat closed at 13,153 points, ended at 12,235 points. The year's high was 14,005 points.
Assis said today's rally was a technical rebound following the recent wave of profit-taking, which was triggered by fears of currency devaluation.
"After so much turbulence, investors figured out that the country was the same, corporate prospects were the same and stock prices were too cheap," he said.
Banks, foreign investors and even local equity funds, which played a large part in last week's heavy selling, participated in Tuesday's surge, analysts said.
Asset managers said pressure from retail investors eased significantly and some funds saw inflows of fresh money in the last two days.
But equity analysts do not expect to see the same amount of cash from retail investors in the funds from now on.
"Many individuals got scared by the bolsa's plunge and will think twice before they put their money back in the funds," said the head of the equities desk at a Brazilian investment bank.

In the first half of the year, retail investors contributed to boost stock funds, accounting for about 13 percent the Brazilian fund industry from just four percent late December. Such investors were non-traditional participants in the bolsa and were only lured into equities by the amazing gains the stock market has made since the beginning of 1997.

Analysts added they were pleased that Brazil's Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) had concluded there was no price manipulation in the market last week. Some newspapers had posited that manipulation was behind the volatility.
